events.label: Nitehawk: The Last Waltz — Classic Pictures
events.desc: Seventeen years after joining forces as the backing band for rockabilly cult hero Ronnie Hawkins, Canadian roots rockers The Band call it quits with a lavish farewell show at San Francisco’s Winterland Ballroom on Nov. 25, 1976. Filmed by Martin Scorsese, this documentary features standout performances by rock legends such as Bob Dylan, Van Morrison, Eric Clapton, Joni Mitchell and Muddy Waters, as well as interviews tracing the group’s history and discussing road life. (Directed by Martin Scorsese, 1978, 117 min., DCP, Rated PG.) Film series: Classic Pictures / Brunch Movies. Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com.

events.label: Nitehawk: Beginners — The Anniversary Party
events.desc: Starring: Ewan McGregor, Mélanie Laurent, Christopher Plummer, Goran Visnjic, Mary Page Keller, Kai Lennox Mike Mills’ Beginners imaginatively explores the hilarity, confusion, and surprises of love through the evolving consciousness of Oliver (Ewan McGregor). Oliver meets the irreverent and unpredictable Anna (Mélanie Laurent) only months after his father Hal Fields (Christopher Plummer) has passed away. This new love floods Oliver with memories of his father, who, following the death of his wife of 45 years, came out of the closet at age 75 to live a full, energized, and wonderfully tumultuous gay life – which included a younger boyfriend, Andy (Goran Visnjic). The upheavals of Hal’s new honesty, by turns funny and moving, brought father and son closer than they’d ever been able to be. Now Oliver endeavors to love Anna with all the bravery, humor, and hope that his father taught him. (Directed by Mike Mills, 2011, 105 min., DCP, Rated R.) Film series: The Anniversary Party / Brunch Movies. Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com.

events.label: Nitehawk: Millennium Actress — Anime After Dark
events.desc: Starring: Miyoko Shôji, Shôzô Îzuka, Mami Koyama Experience the gorgeous new restoration of what many believe to be Satoshi Kon’s ( Perfect Blue, Paprika, Tokyo Godfathers ) greatest work, Millennium Actress . When the legendary Ginei Studios shuts down, filmmaker Genya Tachibana and his assistant are tasked with interviewing its reclusive star, Chiyoko Fujiwara, who had retired from the spotlight 30 years prior. As she recounts her career, Genya and his crew are literally pulled into her memories where they witness her chance encounter with a mysterious man on the run from the police. Despite never knowing his name or his face, Chiyoko relentlessly pursues that man in a seamless blend of reality and memory that only Satoshi Kon could deliver. Boasting countless awards, including the Grand Prize in the Japan Agency of Cultural Affairs Media Arts Festival, which it shared with Hayao Miyazaki’s Spirited Away , Millennium Actress is a must-see for anime fans of all ages. (Directed by Satoshi Kon, 2001, 87 min., DCP, Rated PG.) Film series: Anime After Dark / The Anniversary Party. Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com.

events.label: Nitehawk: Eyes Wide Shut — The Nitehawk Holiday Show Spectacular
events.desc: Starring: Tom Cruise, Nicole Kidman, Todd Field, Sydney Pollack After a provocative Christmas party hosted by the wealthy and unconventional Victor Ziegler, Dr. Bill Hartford and his wife Alice (played by at-the-time real-life couple Tom Cruise and Nicole Kidman) set sail on a psychosexual journey caught between reality and illusion, jealousy and obsession. When Alice admits to have sexual fantasies about a man she met, Bill becomes hell bent on having an illicit encounter but after he sneaks into a secret society sex party, he quickly discovers he’s in way over his head. With its intimate dialogue and sweepingly vibrant scenes, Eyes Wide Shut is a befitting finale to Kubrick’s stunning cinematic legacy. (Directed by Stanley Kubrick, 1999, 159 min., DCP, Rated R.) Film series: The Nitehawk Holiday Show Spectacular / Brunch Movies. Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com.

events.label: Nitehawk: Bad Santa — The Nitehawk Holiday Show Spectacular
events.desc: Starring: Billy Bob Thornton, Bernie Mac, Lauren Graham, Tony Cox, Brett Kelly, Lauren Tom, John Ritter In this dark comedy, the crotchety Willie (Billy Bob Thornton) and his partner (Tony Cox) reunite once a year for a holiday con. Posing as a mall Santa and his elf, they rip off shopping outlets on Christmas Eve. This year, however, Willie is falling apart. He’s depressed and alcoholic, and his erratic behavior draws the suspicion of mall security (Bernie Mac). But when befriending a small boy brings out his kinder side, Willie begins to wonder if there is still some hope for him. (Directed by Terry Zwigoff, 2003, 92 min., DCP, Rated R.) Film series: The Nitehawk Holiday Show Spectacular / Brunch Movies. Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com.

events.label: Nitehawk: Air Mail — 35mm Screenings
events.desc: Starring: Pat O’Brien, Ralph Bellamy, Gloria Stuart, Slim Summerville, Lilian Bond, Russell Hopton Hosted by Caroline Golum and Cristina Cacioppo Before Howard Hawks’ aviation melodrama Only Angels Have Wings , director John Ford hoisted Depression-era audiences up, up, and away to a cockpit-level view of airmail delivery! Ford’s trademark penchant for the American West provides a perilous backdrop to the surprisingly sensational workaday lives of thrill-junkie postal pilots, centering on a reckless daredevil who won’t let anything – a pal, a dame, or even the Christmas shipping rush! – clip his flight feathers. (Directed by John Ford, 1932, 84 min., 35mm, Rated NR.) Film series: 35mm Screenings / Pre-Code Parade. Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com.

events.label: Nitehawk: Little Women (2019) — Representation
events.desc: Accessibility: Closed Captions, Assisted Listening, Descriptive Audio Starring: Florence Pugh, Timothée Chalamet, Emma Watson, Saoirse Ronan, Eliza Scanlen, Meryl Streep, Laura Dern, Bob Odenkirk Writer-director Greta Gerwig ( Lady Bird ) has crafted a Little Women that draws on both the classic novel and the writings of Louisa May Alcott, and unfolds as the author’s alter ego, Jo March, reflects back and forth on her fictional life. In Gerwig’s take, the beloved story of the March sisters – four young women each determined to live life on her own terms — is both timeless and timely. Portraying Jo, Meg, Amy, and Beth March, the film stars Saoirse Ronan, Emma Watson, Florence Pugh, Eliza Scanlen, with Timothée Chalamet as their neighbor Laurie, Laura Dern as Marmee, and Meryl Streep as Aunt March. (Directed by Greta Gerwig, 2019, 135 min., DCP, Rated PG.) Film series: Representation / The Nitehawk Holiday Show Spectacular. Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com.

events.label: Nitehawk: Once Upon a Time in Harlem — Adventures in Black Cinema
events.desc: A decade after his death, genre-defying filmmaker William Greaves has one last trick up his sleeve with what he considered the most important event he captured on film: a 1972 party he engineered with the living luminaries of the Harlem Renaissance. For four hours, this extraordinary group – many of whom had not seen each other in fifty years – reminisced, critiqued, argued, laughed and drank while wrestling with their place in a rapidly shifting cultural landscape. Shot on 16mm film, newly restored and now directed by Greaves’ son David, this landmark film is at once a self-exploration and an inquiry into the heart of the critical mass of energy called the Harlem Renaissance. William Greaves’ intent was not only to document these artists and intellectuals as they spoke about their lives and work but also to plumb the meaning of the extraordinary creative period in which they lived to help us better understand how culture has been passed on from one generation to another and the role that the artist plays in keeping it alive. (Directed by David Greaves, 2026, 100 min., DCP, Rated PG 13.) Film series: Adventures in Black Cinema / ICYMI. Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com.

events.label: Nitehawk: Shouting at the Screen — One Nite Only
events.desc: Hosted by Wyatt Cenac and Donwill, with a special guest Preceded by DJ set by Donwill in Trees Lounge The end of an era is upon us. After 15 years of shouting, we have finally lost our voices. So let’s gather one last time to watch a bit of Blaxploitation and point out some of its most utterly ridiculous tropes. It’s been an absolute joy to share these films with you and reframe that boom mic dangling from the corner of the frame, terrible fight scene or overdramatic death within the context of what it actually is: art. Our only hope is that after this event series you are a little kinder to the people at theaters who talk back at films because it just might be one of us jonesin’ for a fix. After tonight may all of your films be shout-less! (85 min., DCP, Rated R.) Film series: One Nite Only. Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com.

events.label: Nitehawk: Elf — Family Friendly
events.desc: Starring: Will Ferrell, James Caan, Bob Newhart, Edward Asner, Mary Steenburgen, Zooey Deschanel Elf is a mix between the misfit story of Rudolph the Red Nosed Reindeer and the “believe in miracles” story of A Christmas Carol but with the added joy of Will Ferrell in an elf suit running around New York City. Starring as Buddy, one year he crawls into Santa’s toy bag as a baby and gets whisked off to the North Pole where he gets raised as an elf. Of course, he’s a tall fish out of water and eventually decides to head to his birthplace to meet his father. What he finds is a family and a city who have forgotten the meaning of Christmas so he sets out to save the holiday! (Directed by Jon Favreau, 2003, 107 min., DCP, Rated PG.) Film series: Family Friendly / The Nitehawk Holiday Show Spectacular / Brunch Movies. Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com.

events.label: Nitehawk: Sundays on Fire: Secret Hong Kong 35mm Feature — Sundays on Fire
events.desc: Warning: Images are not from the movies we’re showing. Trust us, you can’t imagine what we’re showing! A career-making film from the late-90s, this caper flick rarely gets screened, but it turned out to be a landmark for both its director and its stars. An anthem to urban loneliness, job dissatisfaction, and unconsummated romance, it’s as light on its feet as Ocean’s 11 , as stylish as North By Northwest , and as heart-achingly emotional as a Cantopop power ballad. Featuring two of Hong Kong’s biggest stars playing lonely men who re-discover their love of life by shooting at each other, it’s a rousing, ridiculous, over-the-top supernova of fun, that reminds us this holiday season that what we have to be thankful for are Hong Kong movies. (93 min., 35mm.) Film series: Sundays on Fire. Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com.

events.label: Nitehawk: Heat (1986) — 35mm Screenings
events.desc: Starring: Burt Reynolds, Karen Young, Peter MacNicol, Howard Hesseman, Neill Barry It’s a Vegas Christmas with a grumpy Burt Reynolds! Nick Escalante (Reynolds) is a tough guy ex-mercenary wallowing in Las Vegas, where he uses his muscle as a bodyguard for hire. Spending his free time gambling, he is trying to save up enough “Fuck You Money” to get out of the country. When a female friend is brutalized by local bad guys, he can’t help but get involved. A slick and fun ‘80s thriller that you probably never heard of, this might be the third best movie with the title Heat , but between its colorful Vegas setting and its completely absurd villain death, it is a gift you should give yourself this holiday season. (Directed by Dick Richards, Jerry Jameson, 1986, 101 min., 35mm, Rated R.) Film series: 35mm Screenings / Ridiculous Sublime / The Anniversary Party. Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com.

events.label: Nitehawk: Meet Me in St. Louis — Classic Pictures
events.desc: Starring: Judy Garland, Margaret O’Brien, Mary Astor, Lucille Bremer, Leon Ames Meet Me in St. Louis is a classic MGM romantic musical comedy that focuses on four sisters (one of whom is the nonpareil Judy Garland) on the cusp of the 1904 St. Louis World’s Fair. The film spotlights the sisters’ education in the ways of the world, which includes, but isn’t limited to, learning about life and love, courtesy of the prototypical boy next door. In the end, love — accompanied by song, dance and period costumes, all in glorious Technicolor — conquers all. (Directed by Vincente Minnelli, 1944, 113 min., DCP, Rated NR.) Film series: Classic Pictures / The Nitehawk Holiday Show Spectacular / Brunch Movies. Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com.

events.label: Nitehawk: Gremlins — The Nitehawk Holiday Show Spectacular
events.desc: Starring: Zach Galligan, Hoyt Axton, Frances Lee McCain, Phoebe Cates, Polly Holliday, Scott Brady, Corey Feldman, Dick Miller There are only three rules to abide when owning a Mogwai: keep them away from bright light, never make them wet and never, ever feed them after midnight. So when young Peter accidentally breaks two of the three rules with cutie pie pre-Christmas present Gizmo, he unleashes an ugly copy of terrorizers known as Gremlins. As they are designed to do, the Gremlins wreak havoc upon Pete’s small town and have a particular interest in electronics and mechanical devices. Consider this movie the ultimate pet-ownership guide. (Directed by Joe Dante, 1984, 106 min., DCP, Rated PG.) Film series: The Nitehawk Holiday Show Spectacular / Brunch Movies. Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com.

events.label: Nitehawk: A Christmas Story — Family Friendly
events.desc: Starring: Peter Billingsley, Darren McGavin, Melinda Dillon, Ian Petrella While Bob Clark holds a special place in our dark hearts for his inventive horror flicks like the scary treat Black Christmas , it’s his contribution to the American canon of holiday classics with A Christmas Story that solidifies him as one of our favorite directors. Quirky family dynamics, a leg lamp, a bunny suit, bullying, swear words and anorexia are all involved in one boy’s quest for a Red Ryder B.B. gun in the 1940s. With such sincerity and deep humor, make a switch from watching this on television this year and see it on the big screen with your Nitehawk family! (Directed by Bob Clark, 1983, 94 min., DCP, Rated PG.) Film series: Family Friendly / The Nitehawk Holiday Show Spectacular / Brunch Movies. Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com.

events.label: Nitehawk: The Shining — The Nitehawk Holiday Show Spectacular
events.desc: Starring: Jack Nicholson, Shelley Duvall, Danny Lloyd, Scatman Crothers Stanley Kubrick’s filmic version of Stephen King’s novel The Shining is the most beautiful mash up of terror that includes architecture, madness, a time/space collapse, and surreal imagery. The Shining takes place essentially in one place, The Overlook Hotel, that Jack Torrance (starring Here’s Johnny! Jack Nicholson) shares with his wife and psychic son as caretakers for the winter. It doesn’t take long for the hotel to consume his thoughts and propel him to do the unthinkable…murder his family. (Directed by Stanley Kubrick, 1980, 146 min., DCP, Rated R.) Film series: The Nitehawk Holiday Show Spectacular. Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com.

events.label: Gold Leaf (through Dec 6)

events.label: Nature Journaling: Nests and Dreys
events.desc: Do you feel like you need a moment of pause and a deeper connection with nature? Join us on the first Saturday of each month for a free nature journaling workshop, as part of our Peace In Nature series. events.label: Bargemusic Concerts
events.desc: For nearly 50 years, Bargemusic has been committed to attracting local audiences and enhancing the cultural life of New York by offering performances of chamber music in an intimate setting – the type of setting in which chamber music is meant to be heard. To make this experience available to as many people as possible, all Bargemusic Concerts are Admission Free. Check the Bargemusic website for details on the performance scheduled for each day. Bargemusic concerts are 1 to 1.5 hours, with no intermission. Doors open 20 minutes before the concert (no tickets, no reservations). No food or drink

events.label: Nature Storytime
events.desc: Join for Nature Storytime at the Environmental Education Center! Held at 3:00 PM on the third Thursday of every month (during Open Hours ). Librarians from Brooklyn Public Library Adams Street location lead for an exciting and engaging storytime session, along with singing and rhymes. Each month they select a book to pair with the Education Center’s monthly nature theme. Stick around after to check out all the animals and activities in the room during Open Hours! Storytime is typically about a half hour long.

events.desc: Explore Brooklyn Bridge Park like never before during open hours at the Environmental Education Center. The Environmental Education Center is open for free, drop-in hours at 99 Plymouth Street in Dumbo, Brooklyn! Get to know Brooklyn Bridge Park with monthly educational themes, a 250 gallon aquarium filled with critters from the East River, a 10’ scale model of Brooklyn Bridge Park, crafts, a reading corner, and much more. Open Hours offer the opportunity for self-led investigation with guidance by expert educators to reveal the hidden stories found within and around Brooklyn Bridge Park. Don’

events.label: Nitehawk Film Series: The Last Waltz and Beginners
events.location: Nitehawk Cinema Prospect Park, 188 Prospect Park West, Brooklyn, NY, 11215
events.desc: The Last Waltz — Classic Pictures, 11:00 AMSeventeen years after joining forces as the backing band for rockabilly cult hero Ronnie Hawkins, Canadian roots rockers The Band call it quits with a lavish farewell show at San Francisco’s Winterland Ballroom on Nov. 25, 1976. Filmed by Martin Scorsese, this documentary features standout performances by rock legends such as Bob Dylan, Van Morrison, Eric Clapton, Joni Mitchell and Muddy Waters, as well as interviews tracing the group’s history and discussing road life. (Directed by Martin Scorsese, 1978, 117 min., DCP, Rated PG.) Film series: Classic Pictures / Brunch Movies.Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com Beginners — The Anniversary Party, 12:15 PMStarring: Ewan McGregor, Mélanie Laurent, Christopher Plummer, Goran Visnjic, Mary Page Keller, Kai Lennox Mike Mills’ Beginners imaginatively explores the hilarity, confusion, and surprises of love through the evolving consciousness of Oliver (Ewan McGregor). Oliver meets the irreverent and unpredictable Anna (Mélanie Laurent) only months after his father Hal Fields (Christopher Plummer) has passed away. This new love floods Oliver with memories of his father, who, following the death of his wife of 45 years, came out of the closet at age 75 to live a full, energized, and wonderfully tumultuous gay life – which included a younger boyfriend, Andy (Goran Visnjic). The upheavals of Hal’s new honesty, by turns funny and moving, brought father and son closer than they’d ever been able to be. Now Oliver endeavors to love Anna with all the bravery, humor, and hope that his father taught him. (Directed by Mike Mills, 2010, 105 min., DCP, Rated R.) Film series: The Anniversary Party / Brunch Movies.Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com

events.location: Gowanus Dredgers Canoe Club Boathouse, 165 2nd St, Brooklyn, NY, 11231, United States
events.desc: Keep jamming throughout the winter at the Gowanus Dredgers Boathouse. The focus of the winter jam is to work on harder bluegrass tunes in a welcoming group setting. events.label: Refuge with Nora Almeida, Alma Hutter, and Mattie Brubaker
events.location: Gowanus Dredgers Canoe Club Boathouse, 165 2nd St, Brooklyn, NY, 11231, United States
events.desc: Join artists Nora Almeida, Alma Hutter, and Mattie Brubaker at the Gowanus Dredger’s boathouse on December 5th from 2-5:30pm for Refuge—an interactive installation made from discarded umbrellas, a workshop, and a social experiment. There will be tea, storytelling, giant pieces of paper, deep breaths, thermic experiments, and (potentially) climate catharsis. A guided 75 minute workshop will take place inside of the Refuge from 3-4:15pm. Register for the workshop or come for autonomous experiments anytime during the afternoon.

events.label: Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit
events.desc: Prospect Park Alliance is collaborating with NewYork-Presbyterian to offer comprehensive sexual health services in Brooklyn’s backyard at Grand Army Plaza every Thursday from 10 am to 3 pm and every Monday at the Parkside + Ocean Avenue Entrance from 10 am to 3 pm. The NewYork-Presbyterian Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit is a safe, inclusive space for people to receive high-quality sexual health services. Learn more about the Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit in Prospect Park or reach out to us at mobilehealth@nyp.org or (929) 923-3543. No insurance or ID is required to receive care. Staffed by a team of NewYork-Presbyterian healthcare providers, the mobile medical unit has an exam room and consult room, and offers routine laboratory testing, vaccinations, and PrEP and PEP medications that lower the risk of HIV infection. Patients can also be connected to social services, benefits enrollment, and local healthcare providers. Other services include sexually transmitted infection (STI) testing, family planning, hepatitis C screening, health education and more. The Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit is made possible through funding from the Dalio Center for Health Justice and the Division of Community and Population Health at NewYork-Presbyterian, and a grant from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

events.label: Birds of a Feather, Count Together! A Family Winter Bird Count
events.desc: Who’s hiding among the bare branches? Who’s splashing in the icy waters? And whose calls can you hear on a chilly winter day? Bundle up and join Prospect Park Alliance for a fun, free birdwatching adventure as we discover the colorful and surprising world of Prospect Park’s winter birds! Inspired by the National Audubon Society’s annual Christmas Bird Count, we’re inviting families to become bird detectives, explore the park, and help count our feathered friends. Since 1900, this beloved tradition has brought people together to observe birds and contribute to research that helps protect them. Every bird counts! RSVP Search for woodpeckers, cardinals, chickadees, ducks, and other birds that spend the winter in Prospect Park. Learn to recognize them by their colors, calls, and behaviors, discover how they find food and shelter during the colder months, and see how many you can spot! Winter Bird Discovery Stations, 12 to 3 pm : Get hands-on with the wonderful world of winter birds! Discover what different birds eat, play bird identification games, and uncover the surprising ways birds stay warm during Brooklyn’s coldest months. Bird Detectives, 12 to 4 pm : Become a bird detective and explore Prospect Park at your own pace! Pick up a bird detective activity sheet and set off with your family to look for birds, listen for their calls, and discover clues about where they find food, shelter, and places to rest. How many birds can you spot? Winter Bird Count Walks, 1 pm and 3 pm : Bundle up and join Alliance Naturalists for a guided birdwatching adventure through Prospect Park! Search for winter birds, learn to recognize them, and help count the birds we spot along the way. Binoculars will be available to borrow. All ages and experience levels are welcome. No birdwatching experience or special equipment is needed. Just bring your curiosity and dress warmly for outdoor activities!

events.label: Winter Recess in Prospect Park
events.desc: Make the most of winter break with a wild adventure in Prospect Park! Who’s hiding beneath the leaves? Which animals are still active in the cold? And how do plants and wildlife survive the winter? Join Prospect Park Alliance for free, family-friendly nature activities and discover a whole new side of Brooklyn’s backyard! Nature Around Us, 12–3 pm: Winter is full of surprises! Explore hands-on discovery stations, play nature games, and uncover the secrets of plants and animals during the coldest months. Investigate animal tracks, discover where wildlife finds food and shelter, and learn how trees and other plants prepare for spring. Nature Detectives, 2–3 pm: Put your detective skills to the test! Join Alliance Naturalists to investigate the animals in our collection and look for signs of wildlife outdoors. Observe how animals move and behave, discover clues about their habitats, and see what you can uncover about the creatures that share our park. Family Nature Walk, 3–4 pm: Bundle up and head outdoors with Alliance Naturalists for a winter adventure! Explore Prospect Park’s trails, search for birds and other wildlife, and discover the surprising signs of life all around us. Every season brings something new to explore! This program departs from the Boathouse promptly at 3 pm. All ages and experience levels are welcome. Dress warmly and bring your curiosity!

RSVP Tickets for this event are recommended but not required and will not be checked at the event. New Year’s Eve in Prospect Park is made possible in part by support from New York University and media partner VisitBrooklyn.com.

The group will cover approximately 1.5–2 miles. Learn more on the Brooklyn Bird Club website.

events.label: Third Life: Ikebana Exhibit
events.desc: Join Flower Heart Alliance and Prospect Park Alliance for Third Life , an ikebana exhibition held each January in Prospect Park, made largely from discarded Christmas trees. The title comes from the life of the tree itself: its first life is in the ground, its second is in the homes over the holidays, and its third, before Mulchfest , is as ikebana, the Japanese art of transforming plants into living sculpture. Then, they are mulched and returned to the earth. RSVP For the second edition, over thirty artists from many schools of ikebana shape evergreens from discarded Christmas trees, along with flowers, into individual works and one large collective piece, accompanied by an original soundscape and a live demonstration. Third Life is presented by Flower Heart Alliance in partnership with Prospect Park Alliance, which hosts the exhibition at the Picnic House. The exhibition is part of Tea Arts & Culture’s Odes to Common Things program, with support from the Ikebana Iwaya Fund.

events.label: Martin Luther King Jr. Day School Holiday in Prospect Park
events.desc: Join Prospect Park Alliance at the Prospect Park Audubon Center, LeFrak Center at Lakeside and the Tennis Center for the Martin Luther King Jr. Day School Holiday in Prospect Park! Nature Exploration, 12–4 PM Prospect Park Audubon Center, Free: prospectpark.org/audubon Make the most of winter break with a wild adventure in Prospect Park! Who’s hiding beneath the leaves? Which animals are still active in the cold? And how do plants and wildlife survive the winter? Join Prospect Park Alliance for free, family-friendly nature activities and discover a whole new side of Brooklyn’s backyard! All ages and experience levels are welcome. Dress warmly and bring your curiosity! Nature Around Us, 12–3 pm : Winter is full of surprises! Explore hands-on discovery stations, play nature games, and uncover the secrets of plants and animals during the coldest months. Investigate animal tracks, discover where wildlife finds food and shelter, and learn how trees and other plants prepare for spring. Nature Detectives, 2–3 pm : Put your detective skills to the test! Join Alliance Naturalists to investigate the animals in our collection and look for signs of wildlife outdoors. Observe how animals move and behave, discover clues about their habitats, and see what you can uncover about the creatures that share our park. Family Nature Walk, 3–4 pm : Bundle up and head outdoors with Alliance Naturalists for a winter adventure! Explore Prospect Park’s trails, search for birds and other wildlife, and discover the surprising signs of life all around us. Every season brings something new to explore! This program departs from the Boathouse promptly at 3 pm. Martin Luther King Jr. Day Holiday Tennis Program , 1–4 PM Prospect Park Tennis Center, Registration Required, $85: prospectpark.org/tennis Geared for both adults and youth, this popular Prospect Park Tennis Center clinic features a fast-paced station drill that focuses on specific skills, including serve & volley, ground strokes, approach shots and offense/defense strategies. events.label: Birds, Binoculars & Brooklyn! The Great Backyard Bird Count at Prospect Park
events.desc: Calling all curious kids, bird lovers, and backyard explorers! Did you know that Prospect Park is home to an incredible variety of birds, even in the middle of winter? Join Prospect Park Alliance at the Boathouse for a fun-filled celebration of our feathered Brooklyn neighbors as we participate in the Great Backyard Bird Count, an annual worldwide community science event. Families are invited to become bird detectives, try out binoculars, explore bird habitats, listen for bird calls, and discover what makes each bird unique. Help us count the birds of Prospect Park and contribute to a global effort to better understand and protect bird populations. Drop-in Activities, 1–4 pm: Binocular Boot Camp: Learn how to use binoculars through playful observation challenges before heading outside to spot birds around the Boathouse. Brooklyn Bird Bingo: Pick up a bird bingo card and search for some of Prospect Park’s winter residents, from cardinals and blue jays to ducks and woodpeckers. Beaks, Feet & Feathers: Why do ducks have webbed feet? How does a woodpecker find its food? Explore the fascinating adaptations that help birds survive through hands-on games and activities. Build a Bird-Friendly Brooklyn: Discover what birds need to thrive and explore simple ways families can help protect them in their neighborhoods, schoolyards, balconies, and community gardens. The Great Brooklyn Bird Count Board: Throughout the event, families can add their bird sightings to a giant community tally. At the end of the day, we’ll celebrate what we discovered together and share how our observations contribute to the Great Backyard Bird Count. Bird Counts, 1 pm + 3 pm: Help us count the birds of Prospect Park! Families can join guided bird counts, record their observations, and watch our community bird tally grow throughout the day. events.label: Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit
events.desc: Prospect Park Alliance is collaborating with NewYork-Presbyterian to offer comprehensive sexual health services in Brooklyn’s backyard at Grand Army Plaza every Thursday from 10 am to 3 pm and every Monday at the Parkside + Ocean Avenue Entrance from 10 am to 3 pm. The NewYork-Presbyterian Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit is a safe, inclusive space for people to receive high-quality sexual health services. Learn more about the Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit in Prospect Park or reach out to us at mobilehealth@nyp.org or (929) 923-3543. No insurance or ID is required to receive care. Staffed by a team of NewYork-Presbyterian healthcare providers, the mobile medical unit has an exam room and consult room, and offers routine laboratory testing, vaccinations, and PrEP and PEP medications that lower the risk of HIV infection. Patients can also be connected to social services, benefits enrollment, and local healthcare providers. Other services include sexually transmitted infection (STI) testing, family planning, hepatitis C screening, health education and more. Learn more about the Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit in Prospect Park or reach out to us at mobilehealth@nyp.org. No insurance or ID is required to receive care. The Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit is made possible through funding from the Dalio Center for Health Justice and the Division of Community and Population Health at NewYork-Presbyterian, and a grant from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.   Events are subject to change, please check the NYP website for up-to-date information .

events.label: Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit
events.desc: Prospect Park Alliance is collaborating with NewYork-Presbyterian to offer comprehensive sexual health services in Brooklyn’s backyard at Grand Army Plaza every Thursday from 10 am to 3 pm and every Monday at the Parkside + Ocean Avenue Entrance from 10 am to 3 pm. The NewYork-Presbyterian Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit is a safe, inclusive space for people to receive high-quality sexual health services. Learn more about the Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit in Prospect Park or reach out to us at mobilehealth@nyp.org or (929) 923-3543. No insurance or ID is required to receive care. Staffed by a team of NewYork-Presbyterian healthcare providers, the mobile medical unit has an exam room and consult room, and offers routine laboratory testing, vaccinations, and PrEP and PEP medications that lower the risk of HIV infection. Patients can also be connected to social services, benefits enrollment, and local healthcare providers. Other services include sexually transmitted infection (STI) testing, family planning, hepatitis C screening, health education and more. The Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit is made possible through funding from the Dalio Center for Health Justice and the Division of Community and Population Health at NewYork-Presbyterian, and a grant from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
